value.rationale: The union of opposite finite parabolas is a canonical reducible quadratic spectral set, and its Fourier-algebra norm measures the exact worst-case ℓ∞ amplification of the associated projection. Unlike a routine single-parabola Gauss-magnitude calculation, the union requires absolute-value interference and yields a sharp universal 4/π enhancement, plus a nontrivial quantitative Fourier-ratio coefficient across infinitely many primes. The formula and asymptotic are precise natural invariants with direct relevance to Fourier projection stability and spectral-synthesis concentration.
